segments.text: Hi, it's Minh again. Three months ago, my copilot fixed Inkwell's AI margin. Here's what happened next.
On October first, we capped Agent runs on the Team plan, and moved most chat to a cheaper model. Margin jumped thirty-two points. Churn went up too.

The rules already cost me twenty-five hundred dollars a month in lost revenue. Since October, every month has a dark red slice: customers who blamed the rules. The savings shrink, the losses add up, and next month they cross.
So, who do I call this week? Churn Radar scores every customer against their own normal. Noah is back. The cap refused three hundred and thirty-three of his Agent runs, and his usage just halved.
The risk score, churn and lost revenue are each defined once, in code, with anfra. Inspect shows the exact query behind the list. And my copilot reads the same numbers.

Raise Noah's cap? That costs more than he pays. Let him pay a dollar per extra run instead, and he keeps working, and I make money. Suggested plays for the whole list keep about five hundred dollars a month, and sixty-four hundred over the next six months.
Or, I just ask. The copilot scores every play, picks the best one for each customer, and sends the offers. Pay per run for the Team accounts, a discount or a check-in for the rest.
Thirteen offers out, billing updated, and the green line is revenue I keep.
Fix the margin. Keep the customers. Churn Radar, built with anfra.
